decisions.reason: After four years and with the product no longer observed on the website in 2020–2021, management would read this as uncertainty having largely resolved without strong enough market traction to justify keeping this hardware option open.

This 2018 surveillance display also disappeared from observation after 2019, so the firm would likely conclude that the learning phase is over and resources are better redeployed to stronger surveillance and integration offers.

An airport systems training program is a low-cost service complement to the installed base, so with limited contrary evidence the firm would keep this option open because it supports customer relationships and broader solution sales.

The airfield ground lighting training course fits closely with the firm's established lighting business and is inexpensive to maintain, making it worthwhile to retain while demand remains somewhat uncertain.

Airport collaboration software is closely aligned with the firm's strategic move toward integrated, intelligent and data-driven airport operations, so management would continue backing it as a promising option.

Because the multilateration surveillance system was launched as a flagship and matches the firm's future direction in advanced airport automation and surveillance, management would be reluctant to abandon it absent clear negative signals.
